findings.title: Per-role worker check cannot be computed from WorkerPool: no worker has a role
findings.claim: The plan's worker threshold is `>= 1 per expected role` (download vs OCR), but WorkerPool stores only `{socket, slots, connectedAt}` and `ready()` copies only `payload.slots`. The worker's ready payload is `{"slots": ...}` with no role/host, so `snapshot()` (plan line 80) has nothing to group by. The only role-adjacent signal is `slots.scan`, and `slots()` returns `max_scan_jobs - running["scan"]`, i.e. it is 0 exactly while OCR nodes are busy scanning. A correct per-role check needs either a `role`/`host` field added to the Python worker's `worker:ready` (a redeploy the plan does not mention) or a `socket.handshake.address` -> `deploy/FLEET.md` private-IP map (not in the plan).
findings.impact: Workers card is either an aggregate that stays green when all 5 OCR nodes are down and 2 download nodes remain, or a capacity-based guess that turns red during a legitimate scan burst -- the page's one question ('which dependency is failing?') gets a wrong worker verdict exactly under load.
findings.verification_command: grep -n 'worker:ready\|slots' server/socket/worker.js python/worker/__main__.py | head; sed -n '1450,1464p' server/socket/worker-pool.js
findings.fix: Add `role` (or hostname) to the worker:ready payload and store it in addWorker(), or map handshake.address against fleet.js; state which, and add a test where the 5 OCR workers are absent while the 2 download workers remain.

findings.title: Prometheus join by private IP makes db-mon-1 permanently red and 9/9 unreachable
findings.quote:
The node table is joined to Prometheus target health by private IP; a target that
is absent is `red` with `"no node_exporter target"`.
findings.claim: The live target set has 9 entries but not the 9 fleet private IPs: 10.20.0.30 (db-mon-1, the NFS/Postgres/Redis/Prometheus host) is absent, and the ninth target is `host.docker.internal:9100` (Prometheus runs in Docker on db-mon-1 and scrapes its host via the docker gateway). An exact private-IP join therefore marks db-mon-1 red while `evidence-fleet.txt:21` records its node_exporter as up, and the top row can never be 9/9. The plan's own Prometheus card simultaneously counts 9/9 up, so the same response contradicts itself.
findings.impact: Admin opens Services on session-1 and sees the data host red with 'no node_exporter target' while Grafana shows 9/9 and the Prometheus card says 9/9 -- the page blames the one node that is up, and the natural next action (restart node_exporter on db-mon-1) is wrong.
findings.fix: Join on the target's exported `nodename`/`instance` label or add a known alias for the db-mon-1 host-gateway scrape; assert a fixture where `host.docker.internal:9100` maps to node id `db-mon-1`.

findings.title: The page already receives worker counts on the socket it already opens; /healthz + snapshot() are a second channel
findings.claim: `slotStats()` already returns exactly `{workers, auth, export, queued}` (worker-pool.js:1538-1545), and the /admin namespace emits it on connect and on every accounts refresh (`admin.js:90,108,160`). `useAdminSocket` already stores it as `state.workers` (`useAdminSocket.js:31,150`) for the same authenticated browser that will render Services. So the plan's section 3.2 adds an unauthenticated `/healthz` handler and a duplicate `snapshot()` to a separate process solely to re-deliver a number the page has live. That also answers the scope's explicit question ('worker counts from the socket process without a new endpoint') in the affirmative, via the existing admin namespace.
findings.impact: Needless edits to the socket process (new unauthenticated HTTP surface returning uptime/worker/account counts) and a mandatory icloud-socket restart at deploy time; zero new operator information.
findings.verification_command: grep -n 'workers:' server/socket/admin.js src/admin/useAdminSocket.js | head; sed -n '1538,1546p' server/socket/worker-pool.js
findings.fix: Render the Workers card and the top-row count from `admin.state.workers`; keep GET /api/admin/health for infrastructure probes only, and drop section 3.2 unless a non-socket consumer (curl/alerting) needs server-side worker counts.

findings.title: S4 has no probe, and its red branch ('last run failed') has no persistent state
findings.quote: | s4 | configured + heartbeat < 10 min | configured, no/stale heartbeat, or env empty | configured and last run failed |
findings.claim: Section 3.1 lists seven probes and none of them is S4, so the green and red branches have no defined source. The heartbeat does exist, but only as per-account files on the NFS export tree: `Scan/s4-manifest.json` carries `"generated"` (s4_upload.py:172-190) and `Scan/s4-complete.json` carries `generated`/`checked` (250-263). A failed upload *deletes* `s4-complete.json` (line 356), so 'configured and last run failed' is indistinguishable from 'no heartbeat' (yellow) -- red is unreachable from the repo's state. With S4 env empty (FLEET.md:34 lists the keys as pending), the acceptance step 'S4 yellow' passes without exercising the check at all.
findings.impact: The S4 row is decorative: permanently yellow on session-1, never red, never green, and acceptance never proves otherwise. The operator learns to ignore it.
findings.verification_command: grep -n 'probeS4\|s4' plan.md | sed -n '1,10p'; grep -n 's4-complete.json\|generated' python/s4_upload.py | head
findings.fix: Define probeS4: read max(*/Scan/s4-manifest.json .generated and mtime) under EXPORT_DIR; stale > 10 min = yellow, unreadable export tree = red; drop the 'last run failed' red or record a per-run failure marker. Add one test with a stale manifest and one with the marker removed.

findings.title: probeNfs duplicates the statfs already on /api/admin/storage, and the plan never names a mount path
findings.claim: `server/admin/storage.js` already statfs's the export/overflow/system disks (`diskOf`, lines 76-85), with a 60 s cache (line 18), and the panel already calls `/api/admin/storage` every 60 s while online (Admin.jsx:279-294, api.js:409-431). The plan adds a second statfs path, a second cache, and presents the 'statfs can block in the kernel' weakness as new when it is already a live request path. It also leaves `dir` undefined: config's default is `EXPORT_DIR=./export` (config.js:150) while the NFS mount is `/srv/icloud` (FLEET.md:5), so probing the wrong directory silently reports the root filesystem free space.
findings.impact: Either a duplicate probe that pins a libuv threadpool slot for the same NFS mount the storage endpoint already touches, or a green 'NFS' card backed by the system disk -- the check answers a different question than the one on the card.
findings.verification_command: sed -n '76,90p' server/admin/storage.js; sed -n '409,431p' server/admin/api.js; grep -n 'EXPORT_DIR' server/config.js .env.example
findings.fix: Export/reuse `diskOf` (or the /api/admin/storage payload) for the Disk/NFS card, state the exact mount (NFS_EXPORT_PATH with a `/srv/icloud` default), and treat 'dir resolves outside the mount' as red rather than reading the root fs.

findings.title: The nginx card's only source defaults to the web process, so nginx down still reads green
findings.claim: The plan puts `nginx via PANEL_URL` in the Edge card (plan line 113) and admits it is inferred (line 160), but section 3.1 defines no nginx probe. `PANEL_URL` is unset in .env.example and defaults to `http://127.0.0.1:3000/admin`, which is the web process directly; the acceptance curl itself uses `http://127.0.0.1:3000` (plan line 143). A probe of that URL answers with nginx dead, so the card reports nginx green on a total visitor-facing outage.
findings.impact: Operator checks Services after visitors report the decoy page, sees 'nginx green', and looks in the wrong place; nothing in the response distinguishes direct-to-web from through-nginx.
findings.fix: Add a PANEL_URL default/warning that requires the public origin, or probe a distinct nginx-served path (e.g. the capture page host) and label the result 'nginx (public origin)'; if PANEL_URL stays 127.0.0.1, drop the nginx row.

findings.title: collectHealth() is not threaded through the router, so the admin-api 200 test runs live probes
findings.claim: The plan's seam is `collectHealth({ env, probes, now })` (line 57), but the route calls it with no arguments and `createAdminRouter({...})` (api.js:125-134) accepts no health dependency. So the test the plan adds to `server/test/admin-api.test.mjs` (line 136) hits the real probes: statfs on the process cwd, TCP to Postgres/Redis, fetch to Prometheus/gate/socket. The router's injected `exportDir` (the temp dir in the test) is also invisible to `collectHealth`, which reads config/env. The admin-api test therefore either blocks on the real NFS/TCP probes or asserts statuses that depend on the machine.
findings.impact: A unit test that fails or hangs on a developer laptop and passes on session-1 -- and a 'collectHealth is injectable' claim that only holds for health.test.mjs.
findings.fix: Add `collectHealth = collectHealthDefault` (or `probes`) to createAdminRouter's options, pass it from app.js, and stub it in admin-api.test.mjs.
